The new standard reflecting plate is designed for radar absorbing materials measurement in the 3 mm band (90-100 GHz).
It uses a truncated pyramid structure made of metal with high permittivity.
Nominal reflectivities of the plates are -5 dB, -10 dB, and -15 dB.
The standard plate dimensions vary with bottom side lengths from 20 mm to 100 mm and thickness from 5 mm to 20 mm.
Slant angles of the truncated pyramid range from 15° to 90°.
The radar cross section formula used is σ = 4πL^4 / λ^2.
Simulation of the -5 dB plate showed reflectivity uncertainty of about 0.7 dB.
Existing Chinese national military standards cover 8-18 GHz and are inaccurate outside this range.
The new plate addresses calibration issues for frequencies beyond 18 GHz, especially 90-100 GHz.
Reflectivity measurement involves comparing reflected power ratios between absorbing material and standard metal plates.
The measurement system calibration process uses both -10 dB and -5 dB standard plates.
The new standard reflecting plate is easy to manufacture and use.
The plate improves calibration accuracy and stability in radar absorbing materials measurement systems.
The standard plate supports the bow test method and space translation method of reflectivity measurement.
The referenced standard plates in the national military standard measure 180 mm by 180 mm by 5 mm.
The new standard reflecting plate has been successfully used by the authors in their laboratory.
Calibration involves aiming the plate with a laser model locator for precise alignment.
The reflectivity of absorbing materials is derived from the ratio of reflection powers measured against the standard plate.
The new plate helps revise measurement system residuals to obtain accurate absorbing material reflectivity.
The development supports the advancement of stealth technology by improving measurement precision.
